newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - April 15.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - April 15.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Tuesday's electronic version of The Wall Street Journal:
* Intel reported better-than-expected first quarter profit results but the semiconductor company made cautionary remarks about its second quarter outlook.
* The Financial Accounting Standards Board (FASB) is considering restricting or getting rid of "pooling of interest," a popular way to account for large stock mergers.
* The Dow Jones industrials closed up 60.21 points at 6,451.90, recovering from an early decline.
* USA Waste agreed to buy United Waste Systems in a stock swap valued at more than $1.5 billion.
* General Motors first quarter net income was better-than-expected, boosted by its strongest performance in North America in over a decade.
* Norwest Corp, NationsBank and First Chicago NBD reported strong quarterly earnings, helped by cost controls, share buybacks and fee growth.
* Coca-Cola's quarterly profit rose 38 percent from a year ago boosted by strong volume growth.
* A merger pact between Enron and Portland General was amended to more than double rate cuts promised to customers in Oregon.
* King World said the company was no longer for sale and it is planning to announce a dividend and a five million share buyback.
* Xerox will unveil a full line of digital black and white copier products which can be upgraded to fax, scan and print PC documents.
* People familiar with the matter say Advanta has given up on legal battles with Visa and Mastercard and is abandoning plans to jointly market a credit card with American Express.
* Montgomery Ward told factors its first and second quarter losses would be much wider than it first projected.
* Lockheed Martin plans to build some parts of Mobile Communications proposed satellite-telephone system.
* Heard on the Street: Don't be so sure about the rebound that traders were hoping for in high-tech stocks.
* Credit markets: Bond prices eased as investors awaited today's release of consumer price data, which probably will set the short-term tone for the market.
